## Before you start {.study}

- **What you need:** Word (desktop, on the web at `office.com`, or the phone
  app) and an AI chat tool that your university allows.
- **Time:** about 60 minutes. Work alone, at your own speed.
- **How it works:** do Steps 1–3 on this page. Each step has a short text, a
  figure and a self-check; Steps 1 and 3 have a simulator. Then do the
  **Tasks to submit**.
- **What you submit:** one Word file with your safe prompts, your tool
  check, the edited AI result and your AI-use statement, before lecture 10.
- **You need Lecture 9:** personal data, settings and rules, copyright,
  honest use.

## Key terms {.study}

{{< glossary personal-data sensitive-data anonymize privacy-settings terms-of-use copyright ai-use-statement responsible-ai-use >}}

## Step 1 · Clean your prompts {.study}

- Find every **personal, sensitive or confidential** part: names with
  contact details, ID numbers, health, salaries, passwords, customer lists,
  secret deals.
- Replace each with a **placeholder**: [Customer], [employee 1], [price].
- Keep what the AI needs for the task; add the real details later, in Word.
- In **Prompt Cleaner**, clean the prompts of **Mona** and **Omar**.

![Anonymize before you paste.](../week-11/images/anonymize.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="../week-11/sims/prompt-cleaner.html" poster="../week-11/sims/prompt-cleaner.png" title="Prompt Cleaner: no personal data in the chat" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Mona and Omar"}
Use Prompt Cleaner. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="keep it: the AI is private|write it in capital letters"}
Mona's table: what replaces "Ali Saeed"?
:   [employee 1]

    Why: A name is personal data; the table needs only a label.

Mona's table: what happens to "diabetes" and "back pain"?
:   they go: the table counts only days

    Why: Health is sensitive data, and the table does not need it.

Omar's contract: why does "Green Hotel" go?
:   it is part of a secret deal

    Why: The customer of a secret deal is confidential information.

Omar's contract: which part may stay?
:   300 tea sets

    Why: The AI needs what is sold to sum up the contract.
:::
:::

## Step 2 · Check the tool, the rules and the copyright {.study}

- **Settings:** Is the chat history saved? Are your chats used for
  training? Switch it off if you can.
- **Account and rules:** use the university or work account if there is
  one, and follow the AI rules of the course or the company.
- **Terms of use:** they say how the tool uses your data and what you may
  do with its output.
- **Copyright:** upload only files that you may share; for a picture,
  check that the tool allows your use.

![Check the settings and the rules.](images/settings.png){width=100%}

![Honest AI use depends on the rules.](images/honesty.png){width=100%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Settings and rules"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a bigger screen|a new password"}
A tool uses your chats to improve its model. What do you do?
:   switch the training off, if you can

    Why: Then your chats are not used to train the tool.

Your university gives you an account for an AI tool. Which account do you use for course work?
:   the university account

    Why: The university account follows the university's rules.

Where do you read what you may do with the output of a tool?
:   in the terms of use

    Why: The terms of use set the rules for the data and the output.

Rana wants to upload the supplier's catalogue photos for a new poster. What does she check first?
:   that she may share them

    Why: The photos belong to the supplier; copyright decides.
:::
:::

## Step 3 · Write an AI-use statement {.study}

- Name the **tool**, say **what it did**, what **you changed**, and how
  you **checked** it.
- Keep it short, specific and true; put it at the end of the work.
- Keep your drafts and prompts.

![An AI-use statement.](../week-11/images/ai-statement.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/statement-builder.html" poster="sims/statement-builder.png" title="Statement Builder: say how you used AI" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The statement"}
Use Statement Builder. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the colour of the text|the price of the tool"}
"I used an AI chat tool for an outline." Which part of the statement is it?
:   the tool and the use

    Why: It names the tool and what it did.

"I rewrote it in my own words." Which part is it?
:   what you changed

    Why: It shows your own work.

"I checked every fact in two reliable sources." Which part is it?
:   how you checked it

    Why: It shows that the facts are true.

"I kept the AI draft as it was." What is it?
:   a warning sign

    Why: An unchanged AI draft is not your own work.
:::
:::

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

Do the tasks alone. Your teacher marks them (6 marks). Open a new Word file
and write your answers in it.

### Task 1 · Three safe prompts (2 marks)

Copy these three **unsafe prompts** into your file. Below each one, write a
safe version with placeholders, and list what you replaced and why.

> **Huda:** Write a kind e-mail to our employee Nadia Khalil (employee
> number 4471, phone 0790 000 321), who is on sick leave with a broken arm,
> asking when Nadia expects to return.

> **Rana:** A customer, Karim Yousef from 8 River Road, complained that the
> tea set Karim bought for 45 JD on 2 June arrived broken. The card ended in
> 4410. Write a reply that offers a new set.

> **Sami:** Here are the grades of my group: Dana 20231187 got 62, Ali
> 20231190 got 48, and I got 75. Write a message to the group about who
> must do more work.

### Task 2 · Check your AI tool (1 mark)

For the AI chat tool you use, write a short table: the name of the tool and
the account you use; is the chat history saved; are chats used for
training (and can you switch it off); one rule about AI from your course or
your university.

### Task 3 · Use a safe prompt and state it (2 marks)

1. Choose one of your safe prompts from Task 1 and use it in the AI tool.
   Paste the answer into your file.
2. Edit the answer: add the real details yourself where needed, correct
   anything wrong, and make it sound like you. Show the final text.
3. Write an **AI-use statement** of three to five sentences: tool, use,
   what you changed, how you checked it.

### Task 4 · Reflect (1 mark)

a) Which part of the three prompts was the hardest to decide (clean or
keep), and why?

{{< answer-space lines=3 >}}

## How to submit

Upload your Word file (the safe prompts, the tool check, the edited AI
result and your statement) to the university e-learning platform, **before
lecture 10**.
